reasoning: Kyle Rodda highlights that Tesla, like Alphabet, saw its shares fall in after-hours trade driven by investor concern about excessive capital expenditure and the risk that it will erode return on investment. He frames this as part of a broader, predominant market theme weighing on large-cap tech and growth names reporting results.
quote: The fear of excess capital expenditure eroding return on investment has plagued both companies again, and we've seen the shares of both Tesla and Alphabet chop a little bit in after hours trade, but ultimately pushed lower.

headline: Middle East escalation rhetoric pushing oil to 5-6 week highs with risk to energy infrastructure
reasoning: Kyle Rodda explains that heated rhetoric between the US and Iran, including threats to attack Gulf state energy infrastructure and the potential activation of the Houthis to block the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, is driving oil prices to 5-6 week highs. He notes markets are rationally responding to language that mirrors the conditions that previously pushed oil toward $121 per barrel when pricing in strikes on energy infrastructure. He cautions that if the rhetoric materialises, supply could be taken offline for extended periods, with flow-on effects to global rate expectations.
quote: The initial threat was effectively that the Trump administration or the United States would start taking out bridges and power plants if strikes continued on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. And, you know, the Iranians have turned around and said, well, you know, Gulf state energy infrastructure is fair game if the United States does that. And of course, all these fears, too, that the Houthis will be activated to block the bubble Mandeb and stop oil coming out of the Red sea... So there's this kind of, I guess, concern here that we're ratcheting up things once again and starting to get to a position that was probably largely responsible for why we saw oil prices hit 12125 at least, you know, at the front end of the futures market... the language itself is enough to kind of, you know, basically push oil prices to a 5 or 6 week high.
